title: Finite surjective affine-source morphisms to algebraic spaces have affine target
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism. Suppose $X$ is represented by an affine scheme, and suppose $f$ is finite on scheme tests: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and morphism $T\to Y$, the sheaf fibre product $X\times_YT$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is represented by a scheme and its projection to $T$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Suppose the map $|f|:|X|\to|Y|$ on field-valued point classes with atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] is surjective. Then $Y$ is represented by an affine scheme over $S$. No Noetherian, finite-presentation, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07VS (lemma-affine), full statement. Surjectivity on point classes agrees with scheme-test surjectivity by spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H5 (lemma-characterize-surjective).

proof.text: Finiteness on every scheme test makes every test map proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Thus [lem-sfb-space-representable-proper-tests] gives intrinsic properness of $f$, in particular universal closedness. The affine scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The continuous surjection $|X|\to|Y|$ makes $|Y|$ quasi-compact: pull any open cover back to $X$ and take a finite subcover. By [lem-sfb-space-uc-surjection-separation], $Y$ is quasi-separated. Use [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to view both spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Its coproduct formula identifies each new scheme-test fibre with the original test fibre for the induced map to $S$, and its unchanged atlas identifies point spaces. Finiteness, surjectivity and qcqs therefore persist.

source.place: Tag 07VS, first paragraph; the qcqs conclusion suffices, without the stronger separatedness conclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-fp-approximation] to write $X=\varprojlim_aX_a$ over $Y$, with affine transitions and finite finitely presented $g_a:X_a\to Y$. Every $X_a$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source]. Since the limit $X$ is affine, [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] makes some $X_a$ affine. The factorization $f=g_a p_a$ makes $|g_a|$ surjective: a point of $Y$ has an $f$-preimage, whose $p_a$-image is a $g_a$-preimage. Replace $X,f$ by this $X_a,g_a$; the target has not changed and now $f$ is also finitely presented.

By [lem-sfb-space-absolute-noetherian-approximation], write $Y=\varprojlim_iY_i$ with affine transitions and Noetherian qcqs stages. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fp-over-space-limit-descent] to the finitely presented $f$ to obtain a finitely presented $f_0:X_0\to Y_{i_0}$ with $X\cong X_0\times_{Y_{i_0}}Y$. On the directed tail $i\geq i_0$ set $X_i=X_0\times_{Y_{i_0}}Y_i$ and let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be its projection. Finite presentation persists by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], so each $X_i$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source]. Its transition maps are affine by base change [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. Base-change compatibility of limits [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] identifies $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$.

source.place: Tag 07VS, third paragraph, approximation and descent of the finitely presented morphism.

proof.text: The morphism $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type: on every chart a finitely presented algebra has its finite list of generators. Apply [lem-sfb-space-eventually-finite-map] with bases $B_i=Y_i$, stage source $X_0$ and stage target $Y_{i_0}$ to make every sufficiently late $f_i$ finite. Apply [lem-sfb-space-eventually-surjective-map] to the same system to make every sufficiently late $f_i$ surjective; its local finite presentation hypothesis comes from $f_0$. Since $X$ is affine, [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] also makes every sufficiently late $X_i$ affine. Choose a common upper bound of these three indices. Then $X_i$ is an affine scheme, $f_i$ is finite surjective, and $Y_i$ is Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-finite-affine-descent], $Y_i$ is an affine scheme.

source.place: Tag 07VS, third paragraph, descent of finite and surjective, affineness of the source, and Tag 07VP.

proof.text: The limit projection $Y\to Y_i$ is affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. Its target $Y_i$ is affine, so [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] implies that $Y$ is represented by an affine scheme. By the equivalence with spaces equipped with a map to $S$ in [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers], this affine scheme with the resulting structure map represents the original algebraic space over $S$.
